The Main Gate Syndrome, also known as the "Main Gate Concept," is a novel approach to managing mass-casualty victims in surge situations. It involves setting up a semi-evacuation hospital or receiving center where additional surgical teams can assist with trauma care.

This concept allows for open-minded flexibility and close cooperation between surgeons and anesthetists, enabling them to share experience, opinions, and ideas. Additionally, emergency ultrasound exams have been found to be valuable and effective in the setting of mass casualties due to their mobility, reproducibility, and immediate results.

In summary, The Main Gate Syndrome is a new format for managing mass-casualty victims by providing additional surgical teams with access to trauma care resources, enabling healthcare providers to work together more effectively in high-pressure situations.
